mainText: Good morning. Here is your curated AI briefing for Tuesday, August 4, 2026. Spotify announced during its second-quarter earnings call that it is expanding its upcoming AI music project to include a partnership with Merlin, a licensing network representing over 30,000 independent music labels. This project aims to provide a legal framework for fans to create AI-generated covers and remixes of songs, provided they have explicit artist consent. Spotify co-CEOs Gustav Söderström and Alex Norström emphasized that the product is designed for existing, consenting artists, contrasting it with services that host fully artificial music. The company intends to offer the tool as a paid add-on, generating new revenue for participating artists. While Spotify did not specify a release date, it confirmed that a research preview will be made available to a subset of users. This move is significant as it provides a sanctioned channel for interactive music creation in an environment where AI-generated content is becoming increasingly prevalent; for context, Deezer recently reported that over 50% of its daily track uploads are AI-generated, highlighting the industry-wide shift toward automated music production. In the realm of autonomous systems, NVIDIA has launched Alpamayo 2 Super, a foundation model designed for robotaxis and autonomous vehicles. The model is built on NVIDIA’s Cosmos 3 Super Reasoner and is now available for commercial use under the open OpenMDW-1.1 license. NVIDIA states that the model is intended to help vehicles navigate complex, rare driving scenarios—often called long-tail events—by providing high-level reasoning capabilities. The company reports that the model outperformed several industry benchmarks, including GPT-4o, in autonomous driving tasks. This release is part of a broader effort by NVIDIA to provide an open model family, allowing developers to fine-tune and integrate their own data for proprietary fleet deployments. By utilizing an open licensing strategy, NVIDIA aims to lower the barrier to entry for automotive manufacturers, as it enables them to deploy sophisticated reasoning tools without incurring the costs associated with training models from scratch or paying for proprietary frontier-model access. Also in developer tools, Hugging Face introduced LFM2.5-2.6B, a small, efficient model designed for agentic tasks, such as autonomous web searching and tool use. Despite its size, the model uses a 128,000-token context window and is optimized for speed, reaching 220 tokens per second on an Apple M5 Max processor. The developers employed a training pipeline that includes agentic reinforcement learning, where the model learns to interact with software environments and tools. The model is now available through the latest version of the Transformers library and is compatible with major inference frameworks, making it suitable for high-volume, on-device agent applications. This development is important because it demonstrates that high-performance, multi-step agentic capabilities can be achieved in small-footprint models, potentially enabling complex AI assistance on mobile devices where memory and computational power are strictly limited. Regarding infrastructure, Texas Governor Greg Abbott announced on Monday that the state will halt new data center projects pending audits by the Public Utility Commission of Texas and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas. The state’s grid operator reports that connection requests have ballooned to 474 gigawatts, with data centers accounting for 90% of that volume, raising concerns that the power grid could be overwhelmed. The audit will require companies to disclose information on water and power usage, as well as their mitigation strategies, as the state seeks to manage the rapid growth of AI and crypto mining facilities. This pause is a direct response to the massive growth in the interconnection queue, which has surged from 233 gigawatts in January; if left unchecked, this demand could reach five times the state’s current peak power consumption, necessitating a shift from Texas’s historically light regulatory approach to more rigorous oversight. In other infrastructure news, NVIDIA announced several storage advancements at the Future of Memory and Storage conference. The company is open-sourcing its cuFile application programming interfaces to improve how graphics processing units interact directly with storage systems.
